abstract: <jats:title>ABSTRACT</jats:title><jats:p>All‐solid‐state batteries (ASSBs) have garnered significant interest as the next‐generation in battery technology, praised for their superior safety and high energy density. However, a conductive agent accelerates the undesirable side reactions of sulfide‐based solid electrolytes, resulting in poor electrochemical properties with increased interfacial resistance. Here, we propose a wet chemical method rationally designed to achieve a conformal coating of lithium–indium chloride (Li<jats:sub>3</jats:sub>InCl<jats:sub>6</jats:sub>) onto vapor‐grown carbon fibers (VGCFs) as conductive agents. First, with the advantage of the Li<jats:sub>3</jats:sub>InCl<jats:sub>6</jats:sub> protective layer, use of VGCF@Li<jats:sub>3</jats:sub>InCl<jats:sub>6</jats:sub> leads to enhanced interfacial stability and improved electrochemical properties, including stable cycle performance. These results indicate that the Li<jats:sub>3</jats:sub>InCl<jats:sub>6</jats:sub> protective layer suppresses the unwanted reaction between Li<jats:sub>6</jats:sub>PS<jats:sub>5</jats:sub>Cl and VGCF. Second, VGCF@Li<jats:sub>3</jats:sub>InCl<jats:sub>6</jats:sub> effectively promotes polytetrafluoroethylene fibrillization, leading to a homogeneous electrode microstructure. The uniform distribution of the cathode active material in the electrode results in reduced charge‐transfer resistance and enhanced Li‐ion kinetics. As a result, a full cell with the LiNi<jats:sub>x</jats:sub>Mn<jats:sub>y</jats:sub>Co<jats:sub>z</jats:sub>O<jats:sub>2</jats:sub>/VGCF@Li<jats:sub>3</jats:sub>InCl<jats:sub>6</jats:sub> electrode shows an areal capacity of 7.7 mAh cm<jats:sup>−2</jats:sup> at 0.05 C and long‐term cycle stability of 77.9% over 400 cycles at 0.2 C. This study offers a strategy for utilizing stable carbon‐based conductive agents in sulfide‐based ASSBs to enhance their electrochemical performance.</jats:p>
